summary: Waren Spacefarer, a young pilot with ten credits, wants forty thousand to buy Marta Okafor's Kestrel. His relief pilot job on Dren Vasko's tug Grubstake turned out to be people smuggling. He alerted customs, disabled the drive, got Vasko to surrender and freed eleven refugees. He gave Inspector Hale an honest statement, filed an informant fund claim (payout months away) and had his cracked ribs strapped. The Vesta job is probably lost. Juno Reyes of Reyes Rapid offers him a three-hundred-credit courier run with medical cargo to Occator Ridge, and hints at steadier, better-paid work afterwards.

facts: Marta Okafor will sell the Kestrel to Waren for forty thousand credits.
Vasko promised Waren six hundred credits on delivery to Vesta.
Waren killed the Grubstake's main drive breaker; the tug can't burn.
Vasko surrendered and wants customs told it was all his doing.
Eleven refugees from the Grubstake hold are now in customs custody.
A customs informant fund pays only after a statement, a conviction and a review, months away.
Waren filed an informant fund claim; any payout is months away.
The refugee woman with the toddler asked for Waren's name.
Juno Reyes offers three hundred cash on landing for medical cargo to Occator Ridge.

recent.narration:
You step past Hale, ignoring her raised hand, and tap four-four-seven-one into the hold pad. The lock clunks. The door grinds open on stale, warm air.

Eleven people blink at the red emergency light: three families, a teenage boy holding a water jug like a weapon, an old man on a bedroll. A woman with a toddler on her hip looks from you to the grey vests behind you, and her face closes.

Hale lowers her voice. "Easy. Nobody's getting hurt." Then, to you, quieter: "They'll need processing. Asylum claims, maybe. Or deportation." She glances at the dead tug. "And you'll need a statement. You're the only witness who isn't in cuffs."

The woman with the toddler is still watching you.
recent.picture: Open cargo hold of an old ore tug in dim red emergency light, eleven tired refugees on bedrolls, a woman holding a toddler staring warily. In the doorway a lean young man in his early twenties, short dark brown hair, light stubble, keen grey eyes, worn olive flight jacket over a grey t-shirt, cargo pants and scuffed boots, beside a woman in her forties, broad build, square face, short cropped black hair, steady hazel eyes, grey customs vest over a dark jacket shirt, heavy boots.

recent.action: Ask Hale about payment for the tip
recent.narration:
"Is there a reward? For the tip?" It comes out too loud. The woman with the toddler hears it. So does Hale.

Hale's eyes go flat. "There's an informant fund. Statement first, then a conviction, then a review board. Months, maybe." She looks you over: the cheap jacket, the bruised ribs. "And asking about money over an open hold doesn't look good in a file, kid."

Behind you, the teenage boy mutters something to the woman. She turns away.

Hale jerks her chin at the ladder. "The cutter's waiting. You can give your statement at Customs. Or you can walk, and I'll remember that you did."

recent.action: Go with Hale and give the statement
recent.narration:
The cutter ride is silent. At Ceres Customs, Hale sets you in a grey room with a recorder and a cup of bitter tea. Her questions come slowly, one at a time. You tell it straight: the job board, the sealed hold, the knocking, the breaker. You don't make yourself look better than you were.

When you finish, she stops the recorder. "That was clean." She slides a form across. "Informant fund claim. It's filed now. Don't hold your breath." Then, after a pause: "A medic's down the hall for those ribs. Free." 

At the door she adds, "The woman with the toddler asked your name. Said you opened the door before we could."

Your ribs throb. Your pocket still holds ten credits.
recent.picture: Bare grey interrogation room at a space station customs office, a lean young man in his early twenties, short dark brown hair, light stubble, keen grey eyes, worn olive flight jacket over a grey t-shirt, cargo pants and scuffed boots, sitting at a metal table with a cup of tea, across from a woman in her forties, broad build, square face, short cropped black hair, steady hazel eyes, grey customs vest over a dark jacket shirt, heavy boots, sliding a form over, cold fluorescent light.

recent.action: Get the ribs checked by the medic
recent.narration:
The medic is a tired man with cold hands. He presses along your side until you hiss, then scans you. Nothing's broken, he says, just cracked cartilage and deep bruising. He straps your ribs tight, gives you a painkiller shot and tells you to skip heavy lifting for a week.

The ache dulls to something you can breathe around. On your way out you pass a job screen in the hall. It's mostly customs notices, but one line flickers: "Pilot wanted. Short-hop courier, Ring Port. Cash on landing."

recent.action: First fill in the informant fund claim form
recent.narration: You sit on a hard bench in the hall and fill in the claim form line by line: name, license number, the tug, the hold code. The clerk at the window stamps it without looking up. "Filed. Don't call us." Behind you, the courier job is still flickering on the screen.

recent.action: Ask about the short-hop courier job
recent.narration:
You tap the listing. A minute later a woman calls the hall screen back: mid-thirties, headset, a dock bay full of noise behind her.

"Juno Reyes, Reyes Rapid. My pilot quit an hour ago." She squints at your license scan. "Licensed, young, cheap. Good. A sealed medical crate to the mining hab at Occator Ridge. Fast skiff, nasty terrain, the landing pad's half a ledge. Three hundred cash on landing."

She sees you hesitate. "It's real medicine, kid. Customs already scanned it. I saw where you're calling from."

Then she adds, "Fly it clean and I've got steadier work. Real money for a pilot who doesn't crash my skiffs."

Bay Nine. She wants an answer now.

action: Take the job, head to Bay Nine
